review: local — uncommitted DLQ rework + deal-stage mapping
effort: high (manual fallback: bundled `qwen review` CLI does not dispatch in this environment; 9 parallel dimension agents + orchestrator verification, machine coverage certificates not issued)
verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES (9 Critical, 14 Suggestion) — all applied 2026-09-24; R1-26 added during the fix pass
suite: 268 passed (the gaps are interleavings the suite never drives; 13/13 targeted mutants documented below)

findings.summary: Create gate now blocks only frozen rows, so a half-succeeded client create (POST commits, then reload raises) is retried as a fresh create — duplicating clients in Aquira.
findings.failureScenario: Approval for hs-9 → POST /Client/Create commits client 501 → update_client_sparse/load_client raises (aquira/client.py:741-745) → item['aquiraId'] never assigned (orchestrator.py:684) → DLQ row aquira_id NULL. Gate (status=='frozen') does not block open rows → poll + reconcile re-POST create up to 5× → ~4 orphan clients; Aquira deactivates, not deletes. The invariant at planner.py:756-757 is left stating the old behavior. Deploy backfill additionally flips historical create-failure rows to open, disarming the gate for them (migration probe: attempts=7 row → create_blocked=set()).
findings.witness: Code trace: create_client raises after commit; orchestrator assigns ID only after return. Probe (real Repo, legacy schema): 'create_blocked: set()' for a pre-existing create-failure row.
findings.suggestedFix: Block unresolved create-failures again: status != 'resolved' (open AND frozen) in open_client_create_failures; update the stale comment with the fix; make reconcile skip (not budget-charge) rows the gate holds.
findings.outcomeNote: Gate restored to block every unresolved create (open+frozen); reconcile now HOLDS create rows with the reason instead of enqueuing duplicate-creating retries; fold backfills ids so a learned aquira_id releases the gate. Pinned by 2 rewritten/added tests; mutation (old frozen-only predicate) reddens both.

findings.summary: innerHTML string-concatenation renders HubSpot-supplied stage id/label unescaped, running fill() on page load of an admin session.
findings.failureScenario: Anyone with HubSpot pipeline-write (portal admin, compromised HubSpot user) names a stage ''; the script runs same-origin as the HubQuira admin → POST /ui/settings (swap hubspot_access_token / aquira_password) or POST /ui/users (new admin). Jinja/tojson escaping is correct everywhere else; only this JS sink bypasses it.
findings.witness: Read of shipped file: el.innerHTML = '<option value="' + s.id + '">' + s.label + '</option>'; fill() called on load.
findings.suggestedFix: document.createElement('option') + o.value/o.textContent (or server-render <template> option rows).
findings.outcomeNote: Options now built with createElement/textContent + replaceChildren; blank pipeline choice + confirm() added. Note: template JS is not test-pinned (verified by read; no JS harness in this repo).

findings.summary: Reconciler hard-codes whatif=False — the only live-write path that ignores the global plan-only switch every other entry point honors.
findings.failureScenario: compose defaults WHATIF=true; README says leave true; banner reads 'PLAN ONLY — no writes'. Under that state the new job queues live targeted syncs (writes to HubSpot/Aquira) with no WRITE confirmation. poll.py:48, webhooks, UI manual-run all honor settings.whatif; reconcile does not.
findings.witness: Grep: whatif=False at reconcile.py:59,62 vs whatif=bool(settings.whatif) at poll.py:48/webhooks; orchestrator gates purely on context.whatif.
findings.suggestedFix: whatif=bool(get_settings().whatif) — and when plan-only, skip the pass without charging attempts.
findings.outcomeNote: run_reconciliation defers entirely while settings.whatif is True (no enqueue, no charge, no budget burn). Mutation of the early-return reddens test_reconcile_defers_entirely_in_plan_only_mode.

findings.summary: Any non-'error' action (skip/notice/archive) is treated as a successful write for auto-resolve, so DLQ rows can close as 'written by sync #N' while the failing field was never pushed.
findings.failureScenario: apply_deal_field_ownership pops pipeline/dealstage for deals without an EntitySnapshot (planner.py:124-142) — true for every deal in a plan-only history — so the retry re-plans as skip → pair appended → resolve_dead_letters closes the still-broken record. The cockpit's core promise (closed = fixed) is violated.
findings.witness: Code: `if str(next_item.get('action') or '') != 'error'` (added in this diff); skip path returns before any HubSpot call.
findings.suggestedFix: Append pairs only for action in {'create','update'} with a real write performed.
findings.outcomeNote: Resolve pairs only for action in {create, update}. Mutation back to != 'error' reddens test_skip_action_does_not_resolve_the_dead_letter_row (which also proves the update contrast case closes the row).

findings.summary: Attempts are charged twice per retry cycle (enqueue + failure), halving the documented budget — and when the freeze lands in add_dead_letter (the common parity), no Teams alert fires.
findings.failureScenario: dlq_freeze_after=5 ⇒ create(1) → mark(2) → fail(3) → mark(4) → fail(5)=frozen inside add_dead_letter: ~2 real retries, not 5, and the alert (which lives only in run_reconciliation over mark_reconciled's output) never sends — contradicting the DeadLetter docstring ('raise one Teams alert').
findings.witness: Instrumented interleave run (probe): 'froze inside add_dead_letter on pass 2: Teams alert NEVER FIRES'. Suite blind: existing tests never interleave a post-reconcile add_dead_letter.
findings.suggestedFix: Charge the budget at one site (failure observation), and route every freeze transition through one helper that raises the alert.
findings.outcomeNote: mark_reconciled is the sole charge and sole freeze path (the one that alerts); add_dead_letter now only refreshes error/schedule/ts-preserving. Pinned by dedup-no-charge test + interleaved-failure assertion in the reconcile cycle test.

findings.summary: stage_map_active is all-or-nothing while the planner substitutes per token, so partially-mapped configurations disable the legacy proposal-stage rescue exactly where it is still needed.
findings.failureScenario: Corroborated by 4 agents. Map won only (or pipeline only) → proposals still emit the literal 'proposal' token → the old ensure_proposal_stage() safety net is now skipped (or it injects the FIRST pipeline's stage id into a custom-pipeline write) → guaranteed HubSpot 400 on every affected deal → mass DLQ inflow + retry churn. One reachable from a single untouched Save click (see R1-9 for why).
findings.witness: Orchestrator:722-733 vs planner:235-241 truthiness mismatch; test suite covers only fully-mapped/fully-blank (test_coverage mutant m-14 survived).
findings.suggestedFix: Gate on the token it guards: 'not (settings.hubspot_stage_proposal or '').strip() and not (settings.hubspot_deal_pipeline or '').strip()'.
findings.outcomeNote: Apply guard keys on the proposal mapping and the pipeline mapping individually. Pinned by test_won_only_map_still_repairs_the_proposal_stage and test_custom_pipeline_map_does_not_trigger_the_legacy_lookup.

findings.summary: Autodetect swallows any HubSpot failure and persists blank stages while keeping the submitted pipeline id — silently wiping a working mapping into R1-6's broken hybrid.
findings.failureScenario: Token expired / 30 s timeout / deleted pipeline → pipelines=[] → three '' suggestions → persist_settings writes blanks (only None is skipped, runtime.py:101) → custom pipeline + semantic tokens → every deal write 400s. Redirect looks clean; if HubSpot is still down the page renders without a form, so recovery is blocked. Also: no confirm() on a destructive one-click write unlike sibling actions.
findings.witness: routes.py:709-725 flow read; persist_settings None-vs-'' semantics verified in runtime.py; two agents independent.
findings.suggestedFix: Abort (and surface the error) when pipelines/stages are empty; validate all-four-or-none; never overwrite non-empty values with blanks without confirmation.
findings.outcomeNote: Both POST branches fetch pipelines via threadpool first and abort-without-writing on failure; autodetect can only improve (blank suggestion keeps saved value); membership + all-three-for-custom-pipeline validation; confirm() on the button. 3 new route tests.

findings.summary: Two retry targets are structurally dead ends that still charge the budget and then escalate: revenue_period rows carry the synthetic period key, and client rows route through a 'writeback' entity that _wanted discards when sync_writeback is off.
findings.failureScenario: revenue_period aquira_id is '12:2026-01:7' (mapping/revenue.py:89) → no contract matches a targeted pull → empty run counted as an attempt → after ~2 cycles: frozen + Teams 'stopped retrying' for a row never retried. client rows map to ['writeback','companies'] but _wanted (orchestrator.py:158) drops writeback when sync_writeback=False (default) → companies-only pass cannot re-propose the create or write it back; freezing then activates the permanent create block (R1-1's gate).
findings.witness: revenue.py:89 compound key; _wanted probe: entities {'writeback','companies'} → {'companies'} with flag off (correctness agent).
findings.suggestedFix: revenue_period → owning contract id (planner._revenue_contract_id); check the writeback/create gates before enqueue; never mark_reconciled targets you cannot express.
findings.outcomeNote: revenue_period rows retried under the owning contract id; client creates and writeback-while-off rows are HELD (frozen with reason, one alert) with zero cycles charged. Pinned by 2 reconcile tests.

findings.summary: Deploy-time retry storm: the backfill makes every legacy row open AND instantly due (NULL next_retry_at), and the first pass enqueues up to 50 groups of full-tenant HubSpot pulls with no pacing, no is_busy guard, no rate-limit handling, and no coalescing.
findings.failureScenario: First reconcile after upgrade: all legacy rows due (probe: due-2999=[1,2]) → up to 50 × (projection + archived deals + schema bootstrap) per 45-min window; _request has zero 429/Retry-After handling (grep); PollJob skips while busy → scheduled sync starves; rows past budget still consume one final full sync because enqueue precedes the freeze computation. Compound backend split: Postgres sorts NULL next_retry_at LAST (SQLite first), so on the compose Postgres the same rows can starve under limit=50 instead. Timing: naive next_run_time means the first pass lands ~5 h after boot, not +2 min (probe: DRIFT-MINUTES 302).
findings.witness: Migration probe (real _ensure_columns + real Repo); due/enqueue code trace; apscheduler localization probe; 4 agents corroborate sub-parts.
findings.suggestedFix: Stagger next_retry_at in the backfill; is_busy() bail-out; coalesce/cap enqueues per pass; charge only successful, expressible enqueues; order_by(...nulls_first()); aware next_run_time.
findings.outcomeNote: is_busy() bail + ENQUEUE_CAP_PER_PASS=8 + past-budget rows parked without a final sync + only successfully-enqueued groups charged + order_by(nulls_first, id) + tz-aware next_run_time + backfill stagger concerns mooted by cap/busy. 4 new tests incl. the 302-min drift mutant guard.

findings.summary: The dedup bump never backfills newly-known ids: an update failure folded into a create-failure row keeps aquira_id NULL, permanently mis-typing the row for the create gate.
findings.failureScenario: create fails (NULL id) → client later exists, update fails with aquira_id 44 → fold keeps aquira_id NULL → row forever counts as an unresolved CREATE failure once frozen.
findings.suggestedFix: open_row.aquira_id = open_row.aquira_id or aid (same for hubspot_id) — or start a fresh row on identity change.
findings.outcomeNote: Fold backfills aquira_id/hubspot_id; releasing-the-gate behavior pinned by test_fold_that_learns_the_aquira_id_releases_the_gate.

findings.summary: .first() with no ORDER BY over a set that legitimately holds >1 legacy row makes the dedup pick arbitrary; duplicates keep separate budgets and spawn separate retry syncs.
findings.failureScenario: Old code appended one row per failure; migrated DBs hold multiples → attempts accumulate on an unspecified row (plan-dependent on Postgres).
findings.suggestedFix: .order_by(DeadLetter.id).first(), or fold all matches as mark_reconciled does.
findings.outcomeNote: Dedup lookups now order_by(DeadLetter.id) — deterministic lowest-id fold on legacy duplicates.

findings.summary: Migration backfills status but not hubspot_id, so repeat failures of a migrated record bypass dedup and create a second open row for the same company.
findings.failureScenario: Legacy row (id only in payload_json._hubspotId) + new add_dead_letter lookup on the NULL column → new row. Grouping keeps the API cost at one sync, but the one-row-per-record invariant is broken for migrated data.
findings.suggestedFix: In the same migration, copy payload _hubspotId into hubspot_id for client rows (Python pass or json_extract per dialect).
findings.outcomeNote: _backfill_dead_letter copies payload _hubspotId into the hubspot_id column for legacy client rows (idempotent, runs every start). Not test-pinned (import-time migration) — verified by the migration probe path.

findings.summary: aid/hid are unclamped against String(100): an overlong id makes the commit raise on Postgres inside add_dead_letter's caller-side except-pass — the failed write is never recorded at all.
findings.failureScenario: aquiraId originates from HubSpot-side custom property (arbitrary text) → >100 chars → silent row loss (resolution[:255] has the analogous clamp; these don't).
findings.suggestedFix: aid[:100], hid[:100]; log the swallowed exception at the orchestrator call site.
findings.outcomeNote: aid/hid clamped [:100]; pinned by test_overlong_ids_are_clamped_instead_of_killing_the_row.

findings.summary: dlq_retry_minutes/dlq_freeze_after are clamped only at the scheduler cadence — the backoff/freeze math trusts the raw value; repo.py:131 also compares without int().
findings.failureScenario: DLQ_RETRY_MINUTES=0 → zero backoff, full due page every pass; freeze_after=0 → everything freezes on first pass while alerting as 'stopped retrying'; a string slipping past coercion makes repo.py:131 raise TypeError inside add_dead_letter (caller swallows → dead letter lost).
findings.suggestedFix: One helper: max(int(dlq_retry_minutes or 45), 5) / max(int(dlq_freeze_after or 5), 2) used by all five sites.
findings.outcomeNote: Single dlq_budgets() clamp helper used by add/bump, mark, scheduler cadence and schedule; floors tested via schedule test (minutes 1 -> 5).

findings.summary: 'Retry now' does not retry now — in the shipped web/worker topology the web process cannot execute or wake the job; the retry happens whenever the interval next fires (up to dlq_retry_minutes).
findings.failureScenario: Operator clicks Retry now on a held row; nothing happens for up to 45 min (and the first post-boot pass is ~5 h out per R1-9).
findings.suggestedFix: Relabel ('Retry on next pass') and show the scheduled time, or make the pass reachable on demand (worker polls a wake flag / claims rows atomically).
findings.outcomeNote: Button relabeled 'Retry next pass' and the page explains the wait; on-demand wake of the worker left unbuilt (would need a scheduler handle across processes) — deliberate scope line.

findings.summary: status has a Python-side default only, so during a rolling restart an old worker inserts NULL-status rows that every new query ignores while dead_letter_counts displays them as 'open' — self-hiding rows.
findings.failureScenario: web migrates; old worker still mid-sync writes a failure row without status → invisible to due/list/actions forever; badge reads 'N retrying' above an empty table. Related: concurrent first-start ALTERs make the loser crash-loop at import (self-heals on restart).
findings.suggestedFix: ADD COLUMN … NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'; run the NULL backfill unconditionally; per-statement try/except on duplicate-column.
findings.outcomeNote: status column NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open' (migration + model server_default), NULL-backfill + hubspot_id-backfill run unconditionally on every start, per-statement savepoints tolerate the concurrent-first-boot ALTER race.

findings.summary: Job registration is duplicated verbatim in main.py:54-58 and worker.py:243-247; and the six new settings are neither documented (.env.example/PORTAINER.md) nor surfaced in /ui/settings, nor re-schedulable when dlq_retry_minutes changes.
findings.failureScenario: Adding/retuning a job now requires editing both files; the cadence setting changes backoff but not the tick until restart, with no visible channel for any of it.
findings.suggestedFix: Extract app/jobs.register_default_jobs(scheduler, settings); add the keys to .env.example/PORTAINER.md and a reschedule hook mirroring reschedule_active.
findings.outcomeNote: register_default_jobs(scheduler, settings) in app/jobs/setup.py, called from both entry points; the six settings documented in .env.example. Cadence-change reschedule hook deliberately not added (cross-process scheduler handle); documented as restart-required.

findings.summary: Dedup overwrites ts on every repeat (dropping first-failure time) while last_attempt_at is written by three sites and read nowhere; the 'When' column was dropped — 'failing since' is now unobservable.
findings.failureScenario: A weeks-old frozen row is indistinguishable from minutes-old in every surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Don't rewrite ts on bump (or add first_attempt_at), and display one attempt-time column.
findings.outcomeNote: add_dead_letter no longer rewrites ts; the page gained a 'Failing since' column reading it. last_attempt_at writes kept consistent, though it remains an ops detail rather than a column.

findings.summary: Docstring names a UI control ('Re-open frozen') that does not exist; the button reads 'Fixed a setting? Retry all N held row(s) now'.
findings.suggestedFix: Quote the real label or the action name unfreeze-all.
findings.outcomeNote: Module docstring rewritten around the hold semantics and quotes the real control names.

findings.summary: stages_save is async def but calls the synchronous 30-s-timeout deal_pipelines() inline — one click can stall the whole web container (which also serves webhooks) for up to 30 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the handler plain def (like stages_page) or run_in_threadpool.
findings.outcomeNote: stages_save now awaits _load_pipelines_threadpool (starlette run_in_threadpool); no blocking HTTP on the event loop.

findings.summary: {{ row.aquira_id or row.hubspot_id }} renders the literal 'None' for legacy resolved rows whose migrated columns are both NULL.
findings.suggestedFix: … or '—' (see R1-12 for the root cause).
findings.outcomeNote: Resolved table renders an em-dash when both ids are NULL.

findings.summary: Mutation-verified: the new DLQ/stage behaviors are widely unpinned — deleting the gate's aquira_id and entity_type filters keeps all 23 tests green, as do mutants killing schedule_reconciliation wiring (raises → 42 pass), deal_pipelines mapping, the frozen-reset in retry_dead_letter_now, backoff arithmetic, due NULL/ordering, alert count, whatif-never-resolves, and persist_settings' DB-write half (setattr-only survives 42).
findings.failureScenario: 15 specific gaps (representative: test_create_gate.py:96-107 no longer pins the invariant it is named for — the folded test row keeps aquira_id NULL by construction; orchestrator.py:911-921 settings→stage_map glue executed by zero tests; repo.py:253-264 frozen-reset unpinned — the very fix added this session).
findings.witness: test-coverage agent ran 13 mutants; all listed survivors green; baseline 23/268 pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the 10 named tests in the report; a conftest autouse snapshot/restore of the Settings singleton; make tests enter the lifespan (with TestClient).
findings.outcomeNote: Added ~15 pins: hold/park/cap/busy/plan-only/overlay/clamp/backoff-growth/schedule-wiring/deal_pipelines-transform/partial-save/wipe-prevention/keep-tokens/fold-gate/skip-resolve/DB-persist half + autouse settings-cache reset in conftest. Remaining unpinned by choice: due NULL-ordering unit, ts-preservation unit, unfreeze-all through the POST route, and the JS template itself.

findings.summary: Possibly: mark_reconciled mutates identity-mapped stale rows; an operator Resolve (web container, separate connection) landing between due_dead_letters and the final commit is overwritten back to open/frozen, discarding resolution/resolved_at.
findings.failureScenario: Window = up to 50 enqueue_sync commits (~seconds-minutes); not reproduced, mechanism consistent with SQLAlchemy identity-map semantics.
findings.suggestedFix: session.expire_all()/refresh before mutating, or a conditional UPDATE … WHERE status='open' (same statement fixes enqueue-failure charging).
findings.outcomeNote: mark_reconciled and freeze_dead_letters expire cached state before reading and re-check status after the fresh read; the cross-process window itself stays inherently untestable in one process.

findings.summary: The create branch duplicates ENTITY_TO_SYNC['client']'s list inline (drift risk); reuse the mapping and branch only on aquira_id.
findings.suggestedFix: entities = ENTITY_TO_SYNC['client'] in both branches.
findings.outcomeNote: The client-create branch no longer enqueues at all (hold instead), so the duplicated inline list is gone; ENTITY_TO_SYNC is the single source for the retry branch.

findings.summary: Terminology drift after the rename: heading 'Failed record writes' vs nav 'Dead letters' vs alerts 'dead letters' vs badges 'retrying/held'; and the freeze alert lists ≤6 rows with no '…and N more'.
findings.suggestedFix: One term per surface; append the overflow count to the alert.
findings.outcomeNote: Teams alert now carries '…(+N more)' past six rows and the page intro was rewritten in one voice. The nav label stays 'Dead letters' deliberately (it mirrors the /ui/deadletters route).

findings.summary: The worker process applied the settings overlay only at boot, so UI-saved stage mappings and DLQ budgets never reached the process that actually writes and reconciles — falsifying this feature's own 'takes effect on the very next attempt' contract.
findings.failureScenario: Admin fixes /ui/stages on the web container, clicks Retry all; the worker re-plans with boot-time blanks, fails identically, and freezes the row. get_settings is lru_cache'd; apply_db_overlay ran only in main.py/worker.py boot paths (grep-verified).
findings.witness: grep of apply_db_overlay call sites + worker run_forever read by two agents; mechanism identical in both reports.
outcomeNote: Settings-staleness Critical (flagged by two agents; dropped from my consolidated artifact at merge time — recorded here for honesty): run() and run_reconciliation() now re-apply the DB settings overlay, so a mapping saved on the web container reaches the worker's next sync without a restart. Pinned by test_reconcile_refreshes_the_settings_overlay.

suite_after_fixes: 285 passed; 3 mutants (old gate predicate, old resolve filter, plan-only defer removed) each reddened exactly their pinning tests
